fichas.title: Petrol Stations: Area, Services and Location
fichas.summary: A simple petrol station requires approximately 800 m²; stations with additional services normally require approximately 1,000 m², while large service stations require 2,000 m² or more. The station should be easy to enter, clearly laid out, visible from a distance, and close to the road. The text describes vehicle services and recommends a location on the left side of the road when leaving town, away from traffic-light queues and road crossings.
uses: Checking and topping up oil, radiator water, tyre pressures and windscreen washer water

fichas.title: Petrol Station Access, Pump Layout and Vehicle Clearances
fichas.summary: Diagrams show access and exit arrangements for petrol stations, including road-junction guidance, layouts without slowing and accelerating lanes, angled pump-island layouts, and an urban station serving petrol and possibly diesel vehicles. Notes specify access-side conditions for one-way traffic, pump-island spacing, vehicle turning clearances, canopy height, and separation of the fuel-tanker delivery point from access lanes.

Plan of petrol station with sales, food and car wash. Allguth Station, Unterfohring

Architects: Haack+ Hopfner, Munich

Services and location
Car drivers should be able to
fill up with petrol; check the oil
level, radiator water level and
tyre pressures (and top them
up if necessary) and fill up the
windscreen washer water; clean
the windscreen, headlight glasses
and their hands; buy goods; use
the WCs; and carry out various car
care tasks (car washing, vacuum
cleaner etc.). Petrol stations should
be easy to drive into, clearly laid
out, easily recognisable from a
distance and as near to the road as
possible.
The location should be on the left
hand side of the road on the way
out of town and not in the queuing
area in front of traffic lights. Also
unfavourable are road crossings,
in which case a better solution is a
location before the corner with an
exit into the side street.
